title: Bayesian logistic regression with stated priors
summary: The posterior distribution of a treatment's log odds ratio under stated weakly informative priors, sampled by MCMC, with a credible interval, the posterior probability of benefit, and sampler diagnostics.
pinned_defaults: Priors: normal(0, 2.5) on each coefficient, normal(0, 5) on the intercept, stated and justified; a sceptical-prior sensitivity analysis where the conclusion could depend on it.

Sampler: random-walk Metropolis written out in R, 4 chains of 5,000 draws after 1,000 warm-up, dispersed starts, proposal covariance 2.4^2 / p times the maximum-likelihood covariance, set.seed(20261206). In practice use Stan (rstanarm::stan_glm or brms) with the same model and priors.
Reported: posterior mean and SD, 95% equal-tailed credible interval, P(log OR > 0), Gelman-Rubin R-hat, effective sample size, acceptance rate; the MLE beside them.
_python_not_applicable: Bayesian regression is included with a truth check only. Markov chains cannot be matched draw for draw across languages. The control file checks the posterior against a Laplace approximation computed in Python (mode and inverse Hessian), checks R-hat and effective sample size, and measures recovery and credible-interval coverage over the seeds by running r.R.
